title: Suspicious PowerShell Network Activity
description: Scope outbound PowerShell connections on monitored devices and correlate them with published behavior and local incident evidence.
hypothesis: PowerShell used to retrieve a payload may leave a process-attributed network event.
considerations: Filter known administrative scripts and managed automation.
Review the full command line and initiating process ancestry.
Correlate destinations with internal DNS, proxy logs and approved intelligence.
Review the surrounding device timeline before broadening the lookback.

title: GSocket Process Activity
description: Find GSocket tooling in Linux endpoint process telemetry for review.
hypothesis: Known GSocket executable names or command-line references may identify investigated relay tooling.
considerations: Review the parent process, account and working path.
Confirm whether the activity was approved. GSocket is dual-use.
Review network events separately. Process execution alone cannot establish a relay session.

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Phishing Destinations
description: Review network or proxy events for the exact downstream domains Microsoft reported.
hypothesis: Exact destination host matches can identify traffic associated with the documented phishing campaign.
considerations: Correlate matches with mail delivery and user click telemetry.
Use the action field to distinguish blocks from permitted requests.
Review URL paths and Entra sign-ins before inferring credential exposure.
Security scanners and automated previews can generate matches.

title: Quick Assist Process Activity
description: Find Quick Assist executions for triage alongside help desk records.
hypothesis: Fraudulent remote support sessions can start with Quick Assist process activity.
considerations: Check for an authorized support ticket and verify who initiated the session.
Review nearby process and network events for activity after the support session.
A process match cannot establish that a session connected.

title: ARTEX Service Principal Sign-ins From a Reported IP
description: Review successful Entra service-principal sign-ins from a campaign-associated IP Microsoft reported.
hypothesis: A successful sign-in from the published address warrants correlation with app ownership and expected egress.
considerations: Review the service principal, credential changes and resource access.
Compare the source IP with known egress and require independent evidence before escalation.
Check Azure activity and resource audit logs for follow-on actions.

title: ARTEX and WISP Infrastructure in CEF Logs
description: Look for traffic involving IP addresses Microsoft reported around Storm-3358.
hypothesis: Look for traffic involving IP addresses Microsoft reported around Storm-3358.
considerations: SourceIP and DestinationIP indicate which side matched. Check traffic direction and policy action.
Confirm independent evidence before attributing a match.

statements: | where SourceIP in ({ipv4}) or DestinationIP in ({ipv4})
| project {time}, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceAction, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct

title: ARTEX-Associated Remote Connections on Endpoints
description: Review process-attributed connections to reported Storm-3358 infrastructure.
hypothesis: Review process-attributed connections to reported Storm-3358 infrastructure.
considerations: Check process ancestry and file activity around permitted connections.
An address match cannot establish tool transfer, execution or actor attribution.

statements: | project {time}, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType

title: Rapid Network Probing Across Ports and Hosts
description: Look for five-minute bursts touching many destination hosts and ports from one source.
hypothesis: Look for five-minute bursts touching many destination hosts and ports from one source.
considerations: Tune the thresholds against approved scanners, load testing and monitoring.
Burst shape can support triage, but does not establish that activity came from AI.

statements: | where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP) and DestinationPort > 0
| summarize Events = count(), Hosts = dcount(DestinationIP), Ports = dcount(DestinationPort), Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 8) by SourceIP, Window = bin({time}, 5m)
| where Events >= 80 and Hosts >= 5 and Ports >= 12

expected_output: One row per matching source IP and five-minute window.

title: Entra Password Spray Across Accounts
description: Find invalid-password failures across many user accounts from one IP.
hypothesis: Find invalid-password failures across many user accounts from one IP.
considerations: Exclude approved tests and shared egress.
Check successful sign-ins and account changes near the same window.

statements: | where ResultType == "50126" and isnotempty(UserPrincipalName) and isnotempty(IPAddress)
| summarize Failures = count(), Accounts = dcount(UserPrincipalName), SampleAccounts = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 12), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 8) by IPAddress, Window = bin({time}, 15m)
| order by Accounts desc, Failures desc

expected_output: One row per IP and fifteen-minute window passing the account and failure thresholds.

title: One Address Signing In as Many Service Principals
description: Review successful service principal sign-ins across multiple apps from one IP.
hypothesis: Review successful service principal sign-ins across multiple apps from one IP.
considerations: Baseline managed automation and shared vendor egress.
Pivot by service principal ID and check credential additions and Graph activity.

statements: | where ResultType == "0" and isnotempty(IPAddress) and isnotempty(ServicePrincipalId)

| summarize SignIns = count(), Principals = dcount(ServicePrincipalId), Names = make_set(ServicePrincipalName, 12), Resources = make_set(ResourceDisplayName, 12) by IPAddress, Window = bin({time}, 15m)

expected_output: One row per source IP and fifteen-minute window with four or more principals.

title: Key Vault Activity From the Reported ARTEX Address
description: Review secret requests from the address Microsoft associated with exposed application credentials.
hypothesis: Review secret requests from the address Microsoft associated with exposed application credentials.
considerations: Compare operation outcomes and caller identity.
Correlate addresses and timestamps with Entra service principal sign-ins.

statements: | where CallerIpAddress in ({ipv4}) and OperationName startswith "Secret"

title: Rapid Secret Requests Across Key Vaults
description: Look for a caller rapidly requesting secrets across several vaults.
hypothesis: Look for a caller rapidly requesting secrets across several vaults.
considerations: Exclude documented workloads that make multi-vault accesses.
Review operation outcomes and identities before inferring secret access.

statements: | summarize Requests = count(), Vaults = dcount(_ResourceId), Operations = make_set(OperationName, 8), Outcomes = make_set(ResultType, 8) by CallerIpAddress, Window = bin({time}, 5m)
| order by Vaults desc, Requests desc

expected_output: One row per caller IP and five-minute window.

title: ARTEX-Associated Microsoft Graph Activity
description: Pivot from the reported cloud credential abuse address to Graph activity.
hypothesis: Pivot from the reported cloud credential abuse address to Graph activity.
considerations: Compare application and principal IDs with observed sign-ins.
Check response codes and positions in the tenant baseline.

statements: | project {time}, IPAddress, AppId, ServicePrincipalId, RequestMethod, RequestUri, ResponseStatusCode

title: Burst of App-Only Directory Enumeration
description: Look for a cloud principal querying many Graph user or group paths in quick succession.
hypothesis: Look for a cloud principal querying many Graph user or group paths in quick succession.
considerations: Known provisioning and inventory apps may produce this pattern.
Inspect Graph permissions and the associated sign-in session.

statements: | summarize Calls = count(), Paths = dcount(tostring(parse_url(RequestUri).Path)), Successes = countif(ResponseStatusCode between (200 .. 299)) by AppId, ServicePrincipalId, IPAddress, Window = bin({time}, 5m)

expected_output: One row per principal, app, source IP and five-minute window.

title: Storm-0940 ConnectWise Cloud App Sign-ins
description: Review successful app sign-ins for the ConnectWise IDs in Microsoft's Sentinel sample.
hypothesis: Review successful app sign-ins for the ConnectWise IDs in Microsoft's Sentinel sample.
considerations: These app IDs can appear during legitimate backup operations.
Prioritize reported-source matches and review ownership and expected egress.

statements: | project {time}, ServicePrincipalName, ServicePrincipalId, AppId, IPAddress, ReportedSource, ResourceDisplayName

title: Cloud Application Credential Additions
description: Review additions of service principal credentials or changes to application secrets and certificates.
hypothesis: Review additions of service principal credentials or changes to application secrets and certificates.
considerations: Verify the actor and key dates against an approved rotation or change ticket.
Pivot to successful service principal sign-ins after an unexpected addition.

statements: | where OperationName =~ "Add service principal credentials" or OperationName has_all ("certificates", "secrets", "application")
| project {time}, OperationName, Category, Result, InitiatedBy, TargetResources, CorrelationId

title: Cloud App Role Grants and Directory Role Changes
description: Review audit events granting app roles or adding directory role members.
hypothesis: Review audit events granting app roles or adding directory role members.
considerations: Identify the grantor, target and exact role in the audit data.
Prioritize unexpected self-grants by service principals.

statements: | where OperationName in~ ("Add app role assignment to service principal", "Add app role assignment to the service principal", "Add member to role")
| project {time}, OperationName, Category, Result, InitiatedBy, TargetResources, CorrelationId

title: Storm-0940 Cloud App Mail Access
description: Find successful Graph mailbox reads by the ConnectWise applications in the published Sentinel sample.
hypothesis: Find successful Graph mailbox reads by the ConnectWise applications in the published Sentinel sample.
considerations: Legitimate backup may read mailboxes. Compare source IP and environment history.
Correlate unexpected accesses with service principal sign-ins.

statements: | project {time}, IPAddress, AppId, ServicePrincipalId, RequestMethod, RequestUri, ResponseStatusCode, ReportedSource, ResponseSizeBytes

title: North Korea · Jasper Sleet Sign-in Alerts
description: Find ingested provider alerts for Jasper Sleet sign-in activity.
hypothesis: Find ingested provider alerts for Jasper Sleet sign-in activity.
considerations: This query depends on the provider emitting and forwarding the named detection.
Review affected identity and device evidence before accepting attribution.

statements: | where AlertName has_all ("Jasper", "Sleet") and (AlertName contains "sign-in" or AlertName has "signin")
| project {time}, AlertName, AlertSeverity, ProductName, CompromisedEntity, SystemAlertId

title: North Korea · Sapphire Sleet ProcmacSteal Alerts
description: Find ingested alerts for ProcmacSteal, a payload family reported in Sapphire Sleet's Rust software compromise.
hypothesis: Find ingested alerts for ProcmacSteal, a payload family reported in Sapphire Sleet's Rust software compromise.
considerations: Determine whether the alert was a prevention, detection or test.
Check dependency and build lineage. The payload label alone does not establish actor attribution.

statements: | where AlertName contains "ProcmacSteal" or Description contains "ProcmacSteal" or ExtendedProperties contains "ProcmacSteal"
| project {time}, AlertName, AlertSeverity, ProductName, CompromisedEntity, SystemAlertId

title: Successful Entra Device-Code Sign-ins
description: Review device-code sign-ins for unexpected users, apps and source addresses.
hypothesis: Review device-code sign-ins for unexpected users, apps and source addresses.
considerations: Baseline approved device codes and confirm what prompted authorization.
GitHub-only device grants are outside Entra sign-in telemetry.

statements: | project {time}, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, ResultType, ConditionalAccessStatus, AppId

title: Device-Code Attempts Blocked by Conditional Access
description: Find device-code attempts failing Conditional Access.
hypothesis: Find device-code attempts failing Conditional Access.
considerations: Identify the specific blocking policy in sign-in details.
Look for later successful grants for the same app and user.

statements: | project {time}, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, ResultType, ConditionalAccessStatus

title: Device-Code Grants From Multiple Network Origins
description: Look for successful device-code sign-ins from multiple addresses for one user and app in fifteen minutes.
hypothesis: Look for successful device-code sign-ins from multiple addresses for one user and app in fifteen minutes.
considerations: Check for shared VPNs, mobile roaming and normal tool use.
Review sign-in and token activity before deciding whether it is suspicious.

statements: | where AuthenticationProtocol =~ "deviceCode" and ResultType == "0" and isnotempty(UserPrincipalName) and isnotempty(IPAddress)
| summarize SignIns = count(), Origins = dcount(IPAddress), Locations = make_set(Location, 8), Addresses = make_set(IPAddress, 12) by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, Window = bin({time}, 15m)

expected_output: One row per user, app and fifteen-minute window.

title: ScreenConnect Spawning a Command Shell
description: Look for shell process launches parented by ScreenConnect.
hypothesis: Look for shell process launches parented by ScreenConnect.
considerations: Confirm the technician, session and change ticket.
Investigate unexpected commands on downstream managed endpoints.

statements: | project {time}, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

title: RelayTrap Scheduled Task Activity
description: Find scheduled task events containing two markers Microsoft identified in SCKit activity.
hypothesis: Find scheduled task events containing two markers Microsoft identified in SCKit activity.
considerations: Review registration context, trigger and referenced file.
Correlate with ScreenConnect sessions and nearby registry changes.

statements: | where ActionType contains "ScheduledTask" and (tostring(AdditionalFields) contains "RelayTrap" or tostring(AdditionalFields) contains "TrapWatch")

title: SCKit Run Key Persistence
description: Review Run and RunOnce changes carrying a RelayTrap marker.
hypothesis: Review Run and RunOnce changes carrying a RelayTrap marker.
considerations: Compare the configured path with files on the host.
Review the initiating process and unexpected support activity.

statements: | where RegistryKey endswith @"\CurrentVersion\Run" or RegistryKey endswith @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
| where RegistryValueName contains "RelayTrap" or RegistryValueData contains "RelayTrap"
| project {time}, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName

title: Defender Path Exclusions Near SCKit Activity
description: Review Defender exclusions that reference remote-support staging or RelayTrap.
hypothesis: Review Defender exclusions that reference remote-support staging or RelayTrap.
considerations: Confirm whether an administrator or endpoint policy created the exclusion.
Review files written into newly excluded folders.

statements: | where RegistryValueName contains "ConnectWiseControl" or RegistryValueName contains "CWInstall" or RegistryValueName contains "RelayTrap" or RegistryValueData contains "RelayTrap"
| project {time}, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName

title: GSocket Distribution Endpoint Connections
description: Review process-attributed connections to published GSocket distribution domains.
hypothesis: Review process-attributed connections to published GSocket distribution domains.
considerations: The distribution domains are dual-use. Verify whether the download was approved.
Review process, file and persistence events following the network activity.

statements: | extend DestinationHost = tolower(iff(RemoteUrl contains "://", tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host), RemoteUrl))
| project {time}, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, DestinationHost, RemoteIP, ActionType

title: GSocket Launch From Cron
description: Look for cron starting a GSocket-related process on Linux.
hypothesis: Look for cron starting a GSocket-related process on Linux.
considerations: Correlate the process and account with host-level cron entries.
Renamed binaries may evade this specific name-based pivot.

statements: | where FileName in~ ("gs-netcat", "gsocket", "gsnetcat") or ProcessCommandLine contains "gs-netcat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gsocket"
| project {time}, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

title: GSocket-Related Files in Linux Shared Memory
description: Review GSocket artifacts written to the shared-memory staging area described by Microsoft.
hypothesis: Review GSocket artifacts written to the shared-memory staging area described by Microsoft.
considerations: Check package provenance and approved administrative work.
Correlate file creation with transfer and process execution events.

statements: | where FolderPath startswith "/dev/shm/" and FileName contains "gs-netcat"
| project {time}, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Phishing Messages
description: Look for mail matching the reported randomized outage subject format.
hypothesis: Look for mail matching the reported randomized outage subject format.
considerations: Check whether the message was blocked or delivered.
Corroborate with the sender, embedded URL and campaign reporting.

statements: | project {time}, Subject, SenderFromDomain, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, DeliveryAction, NetworkMessageId

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Phishing URLs in Mail
description: Find reported phishing domains in mail URL extraction.
hypothesis: Find reported phishing domains in mail URL extraction.
considerations: Use NetworkMessageId to look up delivery status.
Corroborate clicks and subsequent sign-ins separately.

title: Certificate Issuance After a Suspected Help Desk Intrusion
description: Review AD CS certificate issuance near a suspicious support session.
hypothesis: Review AD CS certificate issuance near a suspicious support session.
considerations: Forward Certification Services auditing from the CA into WindowsEvent.
Compare template, requester and time against routine issuance and incident evidence.

statements: | project {time}, Computer, Requester = tostring(EventData.Requester), RequestId = tostring(EventData.RequestId), Attributes = tostring(EventData.Attributes)

title: PowerShell Launched by a Remote Support Process
description: Review observed direct PowerShell child processes of Quick Assist.
hypothesis: Review observed direct PowerShell child processes of Quick Assist.
considerations: This is a narrow process-chain lead. Remote sessions may spawn processes through another parent.
Check the host timeline and support records for context.

statements: | project {time}, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

title: Rapid Denied Probes Against a Single Network Edge
description: Find bursts of firewall denies across many ports on one destination.
hypothesis: Find bursts of firewall denies across many ports on one destination.
considerations: Map vendor-specific action values before using the threshold.
Exclude approved scanners and confirm that targets are part of your intended perimeter.

statements: | where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP) and DestinationPort > 0
| summarize Denies = count(), Ports = dcount(DestinationPort), SamplePorts = make_set(DestinationPort, 20) by SourceIP, DestinationIP, Window = bin({time}, 5m)
| order by Ports desc, Denies desc

expected_output: One row per source, destination and five-minute window.

title: Drupal Web Workers Writing Site Settings
description: Find a web or PHP worker writing Drupal's per-site settings file, a lead for the installer abuse described in CVE-2026-132165.
hypothesis: A web worker unexpectedly writing an existing site's settings.php may indicate attempted reinstallation or configuration tampering.
considerations: Scope results to known Drupal hosts and established sites. New installations, deployments and configuration management can write this file legitimately.
Compare its change time and content to the deployment record. Corroborate unexpected database-setting or administrator changes with web and application audit logs.
This covers a subset of CVE-2026-132165 behavior. The publisher does not report settings.php modifications in the live cases cited by the advisory.

statements: | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "php.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php-cgi", "httpd.exe", "httpd", "apache2") or InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "php-fpm"
| project {time}, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256

expected_output: One row per matching file operation, with the host, path, process and file hash when collected.

title: External SMB From Outlook and Nearby System Connections
description: Find attempts from classic Outlook to reach public SMB destinations and check for kernel-attributed attempts on devices with nearby Outlook network activity.
hypothesis: Unexpected public SMB from Outlook, or SMB recorded under System close to Outlook activity, can help triage forced authentication associated with CVE-2026-124194.
considerations: Review the attribution column first. A shared five-minute window with Outlook is a weaker lead because normal Outlook and SMB traffic can overlap.
Exclude approved external file services and validate endpoint, firewall and outbound NTLM records for direction, authentication and whether any connection was blocked.
Correlate the user and device timeline with recent message opens and check the installed Office build. A network event alone cannot establish authentication data exposure.
The query pivots on TCP ports 139 and 445 for publicly classified destinations. It does not measure HTTP or WebDAV behavior and returns up to 256 SMB events per device per five-minute window.

statements: | extend IsOutlook = InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "outlook.exe", IsPublicSmb = Protocol =~ "TCP" and RemoteIPType =~ "Public" and RemotePort in (139, 445) and isnotempty(RemoteIP)
| where IsOutlook or (IsPublicSmb and (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "System" or isempty(InitiatingProcessFileName)))

| summarize OutlookNetworkEvents = countif(IsOutlook), SmbConnections = make_list_if(bag_pack("EventTime", {time}, "Action", ActionType, "Process", InitiatingProcessFileName, "IP", RemoteIP, "Port", RemotePort, "URL", RemoteUrl), IsPublicSmb, 256) by DeviceName, Window = bin({time}, 5m)
| extend Attribution = iff(Process =~ "outlook.exe", "Outlook process", "System or unknown process with nearby Outlook activity")

| project {time} = todatetime(Connection.EventTime), DeviceName, Attribution, Process, RemoteIP = tostring(Connection.IP), RemotePort = toint(Connection.Port), RemoteUrl = tostring(Connection.URL), ActionType = tostring(Connection.Action), OutlookNetworkEvents

expected_output: One row per public SMB candidate, with attribution strength, device, destination, action and Outlook network activity count.

title: GitLab CVE-2026-97229 Vendor Detection Alerts
description: Find Sentinel alerts named after the six exploitation-attempt detections that GitLab publishes for CVE-2026-97229.
hypothesis: A GitLab-published exploitation-attempt detection can surface requests rejected by safeguards, crash evidence or a related error burst on self-managed GitLab.
considerations: This requires the GitLab detections or an equivalent alert integration to write to SecurityAlert. Match the published titles or preserve them as part of the alert title.
The generic Onigmo native crash signal also covers other GitLab/Ruby vulnerabilities. Corroborate with the CI regex compilation stack, related GitLab detections, and the GitLab and Ruby builds.
A rejection or worker crash can be consistent with an attempt. Review host process, file and network timelines independently for evidence of code execution.

statements: | project {time}, MatchedDetection, AlertName, AlertSeverity, CompromisedEntity, ProductName, SystemAlertId

expected_output: One row per matching alert with the named detection, affected entity, alert ID and reporting product.

title: GitLab CI Regex Native Worker Crashes
description: Look for GitLab Puma crash records containing both the CI regex matcher and native Onigmo compilation frames.
hypothesis: A native worker crash in GitLab's CI regex compilation path can support investigation of CVE-2026-97229 even when alerts have not been integrated.
considerations: Forward self-managed GitLab Puma worker errors as multiline CEF records. Preserve the crash header and stack in Message and use GitLab as the mapped vendor or product.

This is a corroborating signal for the CI path. It can also occur with related Onigmo flaws. Check Ruby package provenance and GitLab build because custom images may use a separately updated Ruby package.
Compare timestamps to GitLab Workhorse and application logs, then independently check for execution evidence. A crash never proves successful exploitation.

statements: | where Message contains_cs "[BUG]" and Message contains_cs "regexp_matcher.rb"
| where Message contains_cs "onig_compile" or Message contains_cs "compile_tree" or Message contains_cs "compile_length_tree"
| project {time}, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, SourceIP, Activity, Message

expected_output: One row per forwarded Puma crash with its host mapping and original crash message for corroboration.

title: Ivanti Connect Secure Post-Compromise Capture Artifacts
description: Find forwarded Ivanti events that mention the hidden-directory sniffer or companion credential parser recovered by Volexity after compromise.
hypothesis: The combination of the appliance's hidden capture directory and a rare executable or script name can identify artifacts seen after an exploit chain involving CVE-2026-111357.
considerations: This requires Ivanti appliance process, file or forensic events mapped to CEF with paths preserved in Message or Activity. Standard VPN connection events usually lack those fields.
This is a campaign-specific post-compromise hunt. Matches support investigation of the reported incident pattern and cannot identify which vulnerability was used at a given appliance.

Verify any matching path against approved diagnostics, preserve available appliance and downstream identity evidence, and check Ivanti's guidance on forensic collection. The investigators reported log tampering.

statements: | where DeviceVendor in~ ("Ivanti", "Pulse Secure") or DeviceProduct contains "Connect Secure"
| project {time}, MatchedArtifact, Activity, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DestinationHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DeviceAction, Message

expected_output: One row per matching forwarded event, with the artifact, available device and network fields, and source log message.

title: AWS WAF PHP2Shell Managed Rule Matches
description: Find AWS WAF's exact managed rule IDs or structured managed-rule labels associated with the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.
hypothesis: A PHP2Shell WAF rule match identifies a request worth reviewing for potential attempted exploitation against a PHP runtime.
considerations: Forward AWS WAF events to CEF using AWS as the vendor or AWS WAF as the product. Preserve the matched rule ID in Activity or the AWS WAF JSON log object in Message.
Use the managed rule group's current version. Coverage of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 overlaps, so a matched rule cannot reliably attribute the request to either CVE alone.

Check the final WAF action and corresponding origin logs. A match in count mode may pass to the application, while a block can stop the request at the edge. Neither outcome establishes code execution.

statements: | where DeviceVendor in~ ("AWS", "Amazon", "Amazon Web Services") or DeviceProduct =~ "AWS WAF"
| extend WafEvent = parse_json(Message), MappedRule = iff(Activity in~ ("PHP2Shell_BODY_Extended", "PHP2Shell_BODY"), Activity, "")
| extend Labels = iff(isnotempty(MappedRule) or coalesce(array_length(WafEvent.labels), 0) == 0, dynamic([{}]), WafEvent.labels)

| project {time}, MatchedRule, WafAction = coalesce(tostring(WafEvent.action), DeviceAction), ClientIP = coalesce(tostring(WafEvent.httpRequest.clientIp), SourceIP), RequestId = tostring(WafEvent.httpRequest.requestId), RequestUri = coalesce(tostring(WafEvent.httpRequest.uri), RequestURL), WebAcl = tostring(WafEvent.webaclId), DestinationHostName

expected_output: One row per matching WAF detection, with the final WAF action, client, request, and web ACL when available.

title: MONAI Label Process Writing a Python Startup Hook
description: Find writes to sitecustomize.py by the MONAI Label service or launcher, based on an artifact Amazon Threat Intelligence observed in a Cairn incident.
hypothesis: An unexpected Python startup hook written by a MONAI Label process is a post-compromise lead for CVE-2026-133968.
considerations: Scope results to systems hosting MONAI Label. Review the process command line to verify the writer was the app service. Package installation, approved deployments and administrative tooling can account for some writes.
Confirm the container or host mounted path, file owner and hash. Review Python process starts and any unusual egress after the file event.
This targets one observed artifact. CVE-2026-133968 can produce other file writes. Launchers that hide the MONAI process name and command line require a locally tuned process filter.

statements: | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("monailabel", "monailabel.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(?:^|[^a-z0-9_-])monailabel(?:$|[^a-z0-9_-])"
| project {time}, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

expected_output: One row per matching endpoint file event with the path, initiating process and file hash when collected.

title: Optimizely Web Experimentation Skimmer Connections
description: Match proxy or firewall destinations against the exact domains confirmed in Optimizely's incident report and identify the reported role of each destination.
hypothesis: Contact with Optimizely's confirmed skimmer infrastructure around November 16 is a lead for downstream browser exposure associated with CVE-2026-132224.
considerations: Review November 16, 2026 UTC first and verify the user had a page or project in scope at that time. Some infrastructure is reused, so outside-window matches can be unrelated.
Compare endpoint browsing, CSP reports and application access logs. Distinguish blocked attempts, successful browser access, and any validated exposure using proxy action and corroborating records.
A connection to the reported collection endpoint is a higher-priority lead. Destination contact alone does not establish which site initiated it or whether information was transmitted.

statements: | extend MatchedDomain = case(RequestHost in ({domain}), RequestHost, ConnectionHost in ({domain}), ConnectionHost, "")
| extend IndicatorRole = iff(MatchedDomain == "pay-relay.wordpressadmin001.workers.dev", "Reported collection endpoint", "Reported skimmer infrastructure")
| project {time}, MatchedDomain, IndicatorRole, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DeviceAction, DeviceProduct, RequestURL

expected_output: One row per matching proxied or logged connection, with the exact domain, campaign role, client, and connector action.

title: Cisco Expressway Post-Compromise Python Staging
description: Find the shared-memory package path and numbered working-directory pattern that F6 observed on compromised Cisco Expressway appliances.
hypothesis: Python package staging on an Expressway appliance together with numbered working directories can identify a post-compromise pattern in one CVE-2026-76466 case.
considerations: Requires forwarded Cisco Expressway process, file or forensic logs that retain paths in Activity or Message. Ordinary call and session logs are unlikely to contain them.

Review both artifact types on the same appliance and contrast them with approved maintenance. F6 reports the numbered directories as a possible ARTEX link. Directory naming alone does not attribute activity to ARTEX.
These are post-compromise artifacts from one incident. Corroborate with appliance evidence, the cluster inventory, and the Cisco PSIRT advisory.

statements: | where DeviceProduct contains "Expressway" or (DeviceVendor =~ "Cisco" and Activity contains "Expressway")
| extend ArtifactType = iff(MatchedArtifact == "/dev/shm/pylibs", "Shared-memory package staging", "Numbered working directory")
| project {time}, MatchedArtifact, ArtifactType, DeviceProduct, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, SourceIP, Activity, Message

expected_output: One row per CEF event with the matched path and the accompanying device or network context.
